title: Positron emission tomography plus artificial intelligence to pRedict malignancy in incidental puLmonary nodulEs
summary: In our study, we want to find out how we can better assess the risk of incidentally discovered lung nodules (IPN). To this end, the lung nodules discovered by chance during computed tomography (CT) are analysed for malignancy using a special examination. This enables us to reduce the number of unnecessary CT examinations and biopsies and detect lung tumours earlier. Patients are examined at the Department of Radiology and Nuclear Medicine at the University Hospital Mannheim. Patients with an IPN after a CT thorax examination are additionally examined at the DKFZ in Heidelberg using state-of-the-art scanners. The scanners are very sensitive and can perform dynamic measurements with artificial intelligence. This should help radiologists and nuclear medicine specialists to differentiate well between benign and malignant lung diseases. If they suspect a malignant tumour, a sample is taken and examined. The measures planned as part of the study (PET/CT and biopsy) comply with the current guideline. Measures outside the guideline will not be carried out.

interventions.name: If an IPN with a lesion size of ≥8 to 30 mm is detected during non-oncologically indicated CT examinations of the thorax (e.g. cardiac issues or lung diseases), FDG-PET/CT is performed in accordance with the guideline. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-Patients with at least 1 detected lung lesion (5-30mm) in the CT thorax
-No oncological disease in the last 5 years
Exclusion criteria:
-Lack of ability to be informed
-Legal care
-Lack of consent to the study
-Pregnancy (no inclusion of pregnant women)
